finding.before: option_value removed percentages, euros and arbitrary text qualifiers before computing a scalar. The eight-face probability fixture with A=1/8 percent and B=1/6 incorrectly certified A as probability1/8.
finding.after: The bare-scalar reader removes only a single enclosing math-delimiter pair and otherwise submits the complete expression to its closed arithmetic grammar. Units, percentages, text qualifiers and mixed math/text remain unsupported; no quantity or condition is silently erased. The stale readable_options comment is corrected.

scientific_argument: A percentage includes a factor1/100 and is not the bare displayed coefficient. A physical/currency quantity or conditional statement cannot be converted to an unqualified scalar without an explicit semantic contract. This API carries no such unit/context contract, so it abstains.
conservative_scope: The reader deliberately does not convert percentages or interpret units. A dedicated consumer may later do so only with an explicit and tested contract.

tests.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_qcm_option_value_semantics.py tests/test_qcm_uniform_die_probability.py tests/test_qcm_scientific_abstention.py tests/test_qcm_closed_symbolic_parser.py tests/test_qcm_method_binding.py tests/test_qcm_current_evidence_guard.py --junitxml=/tmp/qcm-option-semantics-targeted.xml
tests.scope: Controlled fixtures only; no real-corpus question execution.

scope_limits: This closes meaning-erasing normalization in the numeric option reader; it does not certify every solver family or natural-language option grammar.
No source question, stored aggregate, historical receipt or human approval is changed.
